question: In which season are Kharif crops grown?
solution:
The correct answer is__ **Monsoon.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The** monsoon season** on the Indian subcontinent begins with the** Kharif agricultural season**.
 
• Typically, Kharif crops are sown at the **start of the first monsoon rains.**
 
• From the **third week of September to October,** the harvesting season starts.
 
• **Paddy, maize, bajra, jowar, soybean, castor, cotton, sugarcane, turmeric, chilly, bitter gourd, guar, okra, brinjal, turmeric, and ragi **are some examples of Kharif crops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabi crops** are those that are raised **throughout the winter months.**
 
• They are sown between** October and November**, and they are harvested between **April and June.**
 
• **Wheat, barley, peas, grams, and mustard** are a few of the important rabi crops.
 
• **Wheat **is the** main rabi crop **in India and is produced in vast quantities.
